title: Normalize input of ``ignore-paths`` for all path types
description:
- [x] Add yourself to CONTRIBUTORS if you are a new contributor.
- [x] Add a ChangeLog entry describing what your PR does.
- [x] If it's a new feature, or an important bug fix, add a What's New entry in
      `doc/whatsnew/<current release.rst>`.
- [x] Write a good description on what the PR does.

## Type of Changes

|     | Type                   |
| --- | ---------------------- |
| ✓   | :bug: Bug fix          |
| ✓   | :sparkles: New feature |

## Description

This normalises the input to the `ignore-paths` config option by creating both a Posix and Windows path from the provided regex pattern.
It does so by adding a new validator called `_regexp_paths_csv_validator` which creates a list of `path regex`s.

Furthermore, it adds a new overload to `get_global_option` for `List[Pattern[str]]` return types, as we did not have that yet.

Closes #5194

+def _regexp_paths_csv_validator(_, name: str, value: str) -> List[Pattern[str]]:
+    patterns = []
+    for val in _csv_validator(_, name, value):
+        patterns.append(
+            re.compile(
+                str(pathlib.PureWindowsPath(val)).replace("\\", "\\\\")
+                + "|"
+                + pathlib.PureWindowsPath(val).as_posix()
+            )
+        )
+    return patterns
+

review_comments.author: Pierre-Sassoulas
review_comments.body: Why disable here ? Do you think ``use-implicit-booleaness-not-comparison`` is a false positive for assert and tests ? I was wondering too, we changed a lot of existing test when implementing ``use-implicit-booleaness-not-comparison``, but I thought it made sense at the time because the fact it's an empty list and not an empty set is an implementation detail.

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body:
I want to check the validator here. Both `None` and `[]` would pass a `assert not` but are functionally different. I can't iterate over `None` without crashing, which normally I would do because I know this should return a list. 

I have not looked at the changes you mentioned but this might actually be a real problem for tests..

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body: This should be possible indeed. Will make a commit in a second!

review_comments.author: Pierre-Sassoulas
review_comments.body: Shouldn't ``None``, 0 or ``""`` be handled by typing and mypy though ? Change are [here](https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/pull/5120/files#diff-aaad72c33b51517ac27fc355b2918789fad5b2a3d74c45a67a87c78ca1522848R138) (and below)

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body:
They should, but `mypy` does not always run if it doesn't consider the "scope to be typed" (or something worded similarly). It think it would be good to explicitly tests for this being a list instead of `None`.

The changes in that PR do not seem to be particularly troublesome, as they just test that "nothing" should have been returned or put into the messages.

TLDR: If `mypy` was invoked with `-strict` this shouldn't be a problem, but in the meantime I think it is good to test for `[]` specifically because `None` would lead to a crash.

review_comments.author: Pierre-Sassoulas
review_comments.body: Right, we're not quite at the point where we can use mypy with strict. And we have a lot of ``Optional[x]`` anyway.

review_comments.author: DanielNoord
review_comments.body:
Last time I checked I got `mypy --strict pylint` under 2000 errors :) `Optional[x]` shouldn't be a problem (I think) although I did at some point consider making a PR with `no-implicit-optional` turned on. But that PR got a little bit too large to be easily reviewable.

In the meantime, I think disabling here is the best way forward.
